media_strategy.selection_principle: Eurovision is inherently a multimodal subject (music + map + scoreboards), so all five channels are used; chart and map carry the analytical weight while video/image set tone and YouTube embeds make the music actually audible without on-disk audio generation.

chart.reason: Multiple ranked, group, and trend findings need precise charts (top 12-point pairs, jury-vs-televote splits, era trends, decade-by-region winners).

image.reason: Two atmospheric images (12-point cards, stage) carry the editorial tone where charts cannot.

video.reason: image2video animates the teaser to give the page a kinetic open without generating a video from scratch.

audio.reason: Audio is delivered via four verified YouTube embeds of real Eurovision performances (Stefania, Waterloo, Conchita, Lordi) - the dataset is about songs and the reader should be able to hear them. No generated audio is created (disk-tight environment + the real performances are stronger evidence).

interactive_or_map.reason: An interactive Leaflet map of Europe with point-flow arcs is the centerpiece, plus a guess-first quiz on the Cyprus->Greece 12-point rate.

media_blockers.reason: Skipped per disk-tight environment instructions; YouTube performance embeds substitute for sonic content.
media_blockers.fallback_des: des_15, des_16, des_17, des_18 (real-performance YouTube embeds)

des_01.label: Teaser - animated Europe arc map

content.prompt: slow parallax push-in over the map of Europe, gentle drift of glowing arcs, soft pulse of light along the brightest golden arc, no camera shake, no text

des_01.brief: Full-bleed teaser at the top of the page: a slowly pushing aerial map of Europe with thin neon arcs connecting countries, two of those arcs (Cyprus<->Greece, Denmark<->Sweden) glowing brighter than the rest. Plays muted, autoplays, loops. The teaser does NOT show any text.
des_01.rationale: The whole essay is about flow between countries; the teaser visualizes that flow before the reader has read a word.

des_02.label: Headline stat callout - 80% Cyprus -> Greece

content.label: of the time, Cyprus gives Greece 12 points

des_02.brief: Large 96px stat above the chart: 80% in golden display, smaller serif label below. Sits as the first thing under the headline, before the chart.
des_02.rationale: The 80% rate is the lead. It deserves the first visual position in the article.

des_03.label: Top 12-point pairs chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing twelves / opportunities / total points

des_03.brief: Ranked horizontal bar chart of the top 12 directed pairs by 12-point rate, with Cyprus->Greece visually highlighted in gold and all others in muted blue-grey. Each bar labeled with both the pair name and the rate; hover reveals the absolute counts.
des_03.rationale: Comparison ranking is the cleanest way to make Cyprus->Greece's 80% visible against its peers.

des_04.label: Guess the Cyprus rate

content.initial_state: Reader sees a single sentence: 'Of the 35 grand finals where Cyprus could vote for Greece, what % did Cyprus give Greece the maximum 12 points?' and a slider from 0% to 100%.
content.trigger: Reader drags slider to commit a guess and clicks 'Reveal'
content.transition: Slider value freezes; the actual answer 80% is animated in next to the guess; the chance baseline (4%) is shown for comparison.
content.payoff: Three figures appear: reader's guess, the actual 80%, and the random baseline of 4%. A line connects them so the reader sees how far Cyprus is from chance.

des_04.brief: A guess-first slider that asks the reader to predict Cyprus's Greece-to-12 rate before any chart is shown. After the guess, the actual 80%, the chance baseline of 4%, and the reader's guess are placed on a single number line for comparison.
des_04.rationale: The 80% finding is most surprising when the reader has committed to a number first - prediction-then-reveal is the strongest framing for this hook.

des_05.label: Europe voting flow map

content.initial_state: A Leaflet map of Europe with country centroid markers and curved arcs between the top 30 sending pairs from ana_14. Arc thickness scaled by total_points awarded (Cyprus->Greece thickest), color gradient from out-of-bloc grey to in-bloc gold.
content.transition: Country's outgoing arcs highlight; tooltip shows top three recipients with sums.
content.payoff: Reader can read the bloc geography by feel - the dense Nordic cluster, the Greek-Cypriot bilateral, the Iberian pair.

des_05.brief: Interactive Leaflet map of Europe. Each country has a marker at an approximate centroid. Curved arcs connect each top-30 sending pair from ana_14, thickness proportional to total points awarded. Cyprus->Greece is the thickest single arc on the page. Hover a country to highlight its outgoing arcs.
des_05.rationale: This is the article centerpiece - the geographic finding cannot be shown without a map.

des_06.label: In-bloc vs out-of-bloc dot plot
des_06.brief: Per-bloc dot plot showing two dots per row (in-bloc mean, out-bloc mean) connected by a thin line, ordered by ratio. Greek-Cypriot row at top with the largest gap (10.98 vs 2.25).
des_06.rationale: The contrast between in-bloc and out-of-bloc averages is the cleanest single comparison for the bloc-voting finding.

des_07.label: Pre/post 2009 reform comparison chart
des_07.brief: Two-panel small multiple: pre-2009 reform on the left, post-2009 on the right. Each panel has two bars (in-bloc, out-of-bloc). The takeaway is the gap shrunk only slightly - the pre/post bars look almost identical.
des_07.rationale: The point of edt_03 is that the reform barely changed the picture; the visual must show that with structural similarity between the two eras.

des_08.label: Ukraine 2022 jury vs televote split chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip with both values + ranks

style.palette: blue jury, gold televote, Ukraine row outlined

des_08.brief: Horizontal diverging-bar chart: countries on Y axis, jury points to the left (blue), televote points to the right (gold). Ukraine's row is outlined and labeled - juries 192, televote 432 - the two longest opposite-direction bars on the chart.
des_08.rationale: Diverging bars make the public/jury asymmetry visceral; this is exactly the chart type for a 192/432 split.

des_09.label: Stefania YouTube embed

content.caption: Kalush Orchestra - Stefania (Eurovision 2022 Grand Final, Turin). The performance whose 432 televote points outvoted the jury 2-to-1.

des_09.brief: YouTube embed iframe (16:9), wrapped in a styled container with rounded corners, soft shadow, caption below. Sits immediately after the diverging-bars chart so the reader can both see and hear the result.
des_09.rationale: A song competition deserves to play the song. This is the most-cited televote-driven win in modern contest history.

des_10.label: Jury-vs-televote rank divergence chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip with country, year, both ranks, gap

des_10.brief: Slope chart showing each entry's jury rank (left axis) and televote rank (right axis) with a line connecting them. Steep upward and downward slopes are the disagreements. Poland 2016 (25 -> 3, the steepest line) is highlighted in gold; Australia 2017 and Sweden 2018 are highlighted in a secondary color.
des_10.rationale: Slope charts are purpose-built for showing rank-to-rank reordering across two sets of judges.

des_11.label: All-time wins by country chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip with most-recent winning year

style.palette: Ireland gold, Sweden secondary gold, others muted blue-grey

des_11.brief: Horizontal bar chart of all 27 countries that have ever won Eurovision, ordered by win count. Ireland (7) and Sweden (6) at the top in gold; the rest descend in muted blue-grey. Each bar labeled with the count.
des_11.rationale: A simple ranked bar is the right shape for the win-count finding; the visual asymmetry between the top two and the long tail is the story.

des_12.label: Sweden's 12-point lead chart
des_12.brief: Top-15 horizontal bar chart of countries by lifetime 12-point allocations received in finals (Sweden 110, Ukraine 83, UK 73, etc.). Sweden's bar in gold, all others muted.
des_12.rationale: Pairs naturally with the wins chart and supports the Nordic-bloc story without repeating a chart type style.

des_13.label: Waterloo YouTube embed

content.caption: ABBA - Waterloo (Eurovision 1974, Brighton). The win that put Eurovision on the global pop map and started Sweden's six-trophy streak.

des_13.brief: YouTube embed of ABBA's 1974 winning performance, captioned, wrapped in the same styled container as the Stefania embed.
des_13.rationale: Sweden's 12-point dominance is partly cultural; the reader should hear why.

des_14.label: Stage atmosphere image

content.prompt: Editorial photo: an empty grand Eurovision-style concert stage seen from the back of a darkened arena, blue and magenta stage lighting, lasers cutting through haze, the silhouette of a microphone stand at center stage, a sea of distant audience pinpricks, dramatic theatrical glow. No text, no logos, cinematic 16:9 widescreen composition, magazine editorial mood.

des_14.brief: Atmospheric editorial image opening the iconic-three section. Full-width inside the article column, slightly bleeding to the edges, with the Conchita and Lordi YouTube embeds beneath.
des_14.rationale: The 'three iconic wins' section is about cultural memory; an atmospheric stage image gives it a tonal anchor that no chart could.

des_15.label: Conchita Wurst YouTube embed

content.caption: Conchita Wurst - Rise Like a Phoenix (Eurovision 2014, Copenhagen). Austria's win, widely framed as a statement on LGBTQ+ visibility.

des_15.brief: Embedded official Eurovision YouTube clip of Conchita's 2014 winning performance.
des_15.rationale: The cultural-memory section needs the actual performances, not just descriptions of them.

des_16.label: Lordi YouTube embed

content.caption: Lordi - Hard Rock Hallelujah (Eurovision 2006, Athens). Finland's only Eurovision victory, won by monsters.

des_16.brief: Embedded official Eurovision YouTube clip of Lordi's 2006 winning performance, sized identically to the Conchita embed for paired layout.
des_16.rationale: Caps off the iconic-three trio; the reader sees three radically different ways Eurovision can look.

des_17.label: Decade x region winner streamgraph

style.palette: Western steel-blue, Nordic light-blue, Eastern gold, Mediterranean coral

des_17.brief: Stacked bar by decade showing winners colored by region. The 2000s column has zero Western Europe (a missing wedge) - this is the visual surprise the section relies on.
des_17.rationale: Stacked bars over decades make the regional shift legible at a glance and let the missing-Western-wedge land.

des_18.label: Score-12 cards image

content.prompt: Editorial photo-illustration: an abstract close-up of two sets of voting score cards with a glowing '12' on each, connected by a luminous arc, on a deep navy fabric backdrop. Cinematic studio lighting, magazine editorial style, no text other than the numeral '12', minimal and elegant, shallow depth of field, no flags, no faces.

des_18.brief: Closing editorial image: two flip-card '12's on navy with a glowing arc between them. Sits above the closing paragraphs of edt_09 as the visual coda for the Cyprus-Greece bilateral story.
des_18.rationale: The closing section is reflective; an evocative image lands the metaphor better than another chart.

des_19.label: Cyprus<->Greece reciprocal pairs chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing a_to_b and b_to_a

des_19.brief: Top-12 reciprocal 12-point pairs ranked by combined mutual count. Cyprus<->Greece (50) at top in gold, Moldova<->Romania (22) second, Denmark<->Sweden (17) third, etc.
des_19.rationale: Closes the loop visually - the lead chart was directed; this one is mutual, showing that the Cyprus-Greece pair is also exceptional in symmetric terms.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial - deep navy and gold, like a stylized voting scorecard
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: visual-first (animated teaser), then alternating prose -> chart -> embed -> prose. Charts appear roughly every 2 paragraphs.
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Use the Leaflet flow map as the centerpiece rather than the usual stat-callout-then-bar-chart rhythm. Audio is delivered through verified YouTube embeds rather than generated tones - the dataset is about real songs and the reader should hear them. The closing image is a still, not a video, to bring the page down to rest after the animated open.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Stat callouts at 96px gold display serif, body Georgia 18px, captions system-ui 13px, section headings 28-36px sans-serif. Subtle gold horizontal rule between sections.
